Jordan Decomposition

Every bounded-variation function splits into a difference of two increasing functions. Drag the probe and watch the identity hold pointwise.

Record the total rise and the total fall separately. Subtract falls from rises to get the current height. The variation function is the running record of rises.

For example, money now in a 🐷 piggy bank is the total 💰 money put in minus the total taken out. Rises and falls are counted on separate tallies.

Examples & Exercises

Assume fff is of bounded variation on [a,b][a, b][a,b].

Prove that with g(x)=Vax(f)g(x) = V_a^x(f)g(x)=Vax​(f) and h(x)=g(x)−f(x)h(x) = g(x) - f(x)h(x)=g(x)−f(x), both ggg and hhh are increasing, so f=g−hf = g - hf=g−h (one direction of the Jordan decomposition).

Vax2(f)=Vax1(f)+Vx1x2(f)(a≤x1<x2≤b)V_a^{x_2}(f) = V_a^{x_1}(f) + V_{x_1}^{x_2}(f) \qquad (a \le x_1 < x_2 \le b)Vax2​​(f)=Vax1​​(f)+Vx1​x2​​(f)(a≤x1​<x2​≤b)
h(x2)−h(x1)=Vx1x2(f)−(f(x2)−f(x1))≥0h(x_2) - h(x_1) = V_{x_1}^{x_2}(f) - \bigl(f(x_2) - f(x_1)\bigr) \ge 0h(x2​)−h(x1​)=Vx1​x2​​(f)−(f(x2​)−f(x1​))≥0
Show proof

  1. First prove additivity of variation: for a≤x1<x2≤ba \le x_1 < x_2 \le ba≤x1​<x2​≤b, Vax2(f)=Vax1(f)+Vx1x2(f)V_a^{x_2}(f) = V_a^{x_1}(f) + V_{x_1}^{x_2}(f)Vax2​​(f)=Vax1​​(f)+Vx1​x2​​(f).

    The inequality ≤\le≤ goes as follows: given any partition PPP of [a,x2][a, x_2][a,x2​], if x1x_1x1​ is absent we may insert it, since the sum can only grow (∣f(v)−f(u)∣≤∣f(x1)−f(u)∣+∣f(v)−f(x1)∣\lvert f(v) - f(u)\rvert \le \lvert f(x_1) - f(u)\rvert + \lvert f(v) - f(x_1)\rvert∣f(v)−f(u)∣≤∣f(x1​)−f(u)∣+∣f(v)−f(x1​)∣).

    A partition containing x1x_1x1​ has its sum split into a sum over [a,x1][a, x_1][a,x1​] plus a sum over [x1,x2][x_1, x_2][x1​,x2​], each bounded by the variation on that interval; taking the supremum over PPP gives ≤\le≤.

  2. The reverse ≥\ge≥: concatenating a partition P1P_1P1​ of [a,x1][a, x_1][a,x1​] with a partition P2P_2P2​ of [x1,x2][x_1, x_2][x1​,x2​] gives a partition P1∪P2P_1 \cup P_2P1​∪P2​ of [a,x2][a, x_2][a,x2​] whose sum is the sum of the two sums.

    Taking suprema on each interval gives ≥\ge≥.

    All suprema are finite since fff is BV.

  3. Now g(x)=Vax(f)g(x) = V_a^x(f)g(x)=Vax​(f) is increasing: for x1<x2x_1 < x_2x1​<x2​, additivity gives g(x2)=g(x1)+Vx1x2(f)≥g(x1)g(x_2) = g(x_1) + V_{x_1}^{x_2}(f) \ge g(x_1)g(x2​)=g(x1​)+Vx1​x2​​(f)≥g(x1​) (variation is nonnegative).

    And h(x2)−h(x1)=(g(x2)−g(x1))−(f(x2)−f(x1))=Vx1x2(f)−(f(x2)−f(x1))h(x_2) - h(x_1) = (g(x_2) - g(x_1)) - (f(x_2) - f(x_1)) = V_{x_1}^{x_2}(f) - (f(x_2) - f(x_1))h(x2​)−h(x1​)=(g(x2​)−g(x1​))−(f(x2​)−f(x1​))=Vx1​x2​​(f)−(f(x2​)−f(x1​)); but Vx1x2(f)≥∣f(x2)−f(x1)∣≥f(x2)−f(x1)V_{x_1}^{x_2}(f) \ge \lvert f(x_2) - f(x_1)\rvert \ge f(x_2) - f(x_1)Vx1​x2​​(f)≥∣f(x2​)−f(x1​)∣≥f(x2​)−f(x1​) from the single partition {x1,x2}\{x_1, x_2\}{x1​,x2​}, so h(x2)−h(x1)≥0h(x_2) - h(x_1) \ge 0h(x2​)−h(x1​)≥0 — hhh is increasing too.

    The identity f=g−hf = g - hf=g−h is the definition of hhh.

Prove the converse: if g,hg, hg,h are increasing on [a,b][a, b][a,b] and f=g−hf = g - hf=g−h, then fff is of bounded variation with Vab(f)≤(g(b)−g(a))+(h(b)−h(a))V_a^b(f) \le (g(b) - g(a)) + (h(b) - h(a))Vab​(f)≤(g(b)−g(a))+(h(b)−h(a)).

∣f(xi)−f(xi−1)∣≤(g(xi)−g(xi−1))+(h(xi)−h(xi−1))\lvert f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})\rvert \le (g(x_i) - g(x_{i-1})) + (h(x_i) - h(x_{i-1}))∣f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)∣≤(g(xi​)−g(xi−1​))+(h(xi​)−h(xi−1​))
Vab(f)≤(g(b)−g(a))+(h(b)−h(a))V_a^b(f) \le (g(b) - g(a)) + (h(b) - h(a))Vab​(f)≤(g(b)−g(a))+(h(b)−h(a))
Show proof

  1. Take any partition a=x0<x1<⋯<xn=ba = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = ba=x0​<x1​<⋯<xn​=b of [a,b][a, b][a,b].

    On each piece, ∣f(xi)−f(xi−1)∣=∣(g(xi)−g(xi−1))−(h(xi)−h(xi−1))∣≤∣g(xi)−g(xi−1)∣+∣h(xi)−h(xi−1)∣\lvert f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})\rvert = \lvert (g(x_i) - g(x_{i-1})) - (h(x_i) - h(x_{i-1}))\rvert \le \lvert g(x_i) - g(x_{i-1})\rvert + \lvert h(x_i) - h(x_{i-1})\rvert∣f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)∣=∣(g(xi​)−g(xi−1​))−(h(xi​)−h(xi−1​))∣≤∣g(xi​)−g(xi−1​)∣+∣h(xi​)−h(xi−1​)∣ (triangle inequality). Since ggg and hhh are increasing, each difference is nonnegative, so the absolute values drop away.

  2. Summing over i=1,…,ni = 1, \dots, ni=1,…,n, ∑i=1n∣f(xi)−f(xi−1)∣≤∑i=1n(g(xi)−g(xi−1))+∑i=1n(h(xi)−h(xi−1))\sum_{i=1}^{n} \lvert f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})\rvert \le \sum_{i=1}^{n}(g(x_i) - g(x_{i-1})) + \sum_{i=1}^{n}(h(x_i) - h(x_{i-1}))∑i=1n​∣f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)∣≤∑i=1n​(g(xi​)−g(xi−1​))+∑i=1n​(h(xi​)−h(xi−1​)), and the two sums telescope to (g(b)−g(a))+(h(b)−h(a))(g(b) - g(a)) + (h(b) - h(a))(g(b)−g(a))+(h(b)−h(a)). This bound is partition-independent, so taking the supremum over all partitions gives Vab(f)≤(g(b)−g(a))+(h(b)−h(a))<∞V_a^b(f) \le (g(b) - g(a)) + (h(b) - h(a)) < \inftyVab​(f)≤(g(b)−g(a))+(h(b)−h(a))<∞ — fff is of bounded variation.

Prove the Jordan decomposition is never unique: if f=g−hf = g - hf=g−h with g,hg, hg,h increasing, then for any increasing uuu, f=(g+u)−(h+u)f = (g + u) - (h + u)f=(g+u)−(h+u) is another one.

f=g−h=(g+u)−(h+u),u increasingf = g - h = (g + u) - (h + u), \qquad u\ \text{increasing}f=g−h=(g+u)−(h+u),u increasing
Show proof

  1. A sum of increasing functions is increasing: if x1<x2x_1 < x_2x1​<x2​ then g(x1)≤g(x2)g(x_1) \le g(x_2)g(x1​)≤g(x2​) and u(x1)≤u(x2)u(x_1) \le u(x_2)u(x1​)≤u(x2​), so (g+u)(x1)≤(g+u)(x2)(g+u)(x_1) \le (g+u)(x_2)(g+u)(x1​)≤(g+u)(x2​) — and the same for h+uh + uh+u.

  2. Then (g+u)−(h+u)=g−h=f(g + u) - (h + u) = g - h = f(g+u)−(h+u)=g−h=f — the uuu cancels.

    Since there are infinitely many increasing functions uuu (e.g. u(x)=xu(x) = xu(x)=x, u(x)=x2u(x) = x^2u(x)=x2, u(x)=2u(x) = 2u(x)=2 constant), there are infinitely many Jordan decompositions.

    Uniqueness would need an extra normalization (e.g. g(a)=0g(a) = 0g(a)=0).
